title: Cognitive-Heuristic Guided Multimodal Data Augmentation for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection Using LLM and TTS
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, and early detection is critical for intervention. Speech offers a non-invasive, accessible biomarker for AD detection, but suffers from severe data scarcity. Existing augmentation methods in text or speech enrich training data but often neglect cognitively relevant patterns. We propose a cognitive-heuristic guided multimodal generative augmentation frame work that explicitly incorporates AD-related cognitive declines. Our method integrates retrieval-augmented generation with large language models for cognitively informed text generation, and an attribute-guided text-to-speech system to reproduce AD-related acoustic features. This design captures both linguistic and acoustic alterations associated with cognitive decline. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our augmented data consistently enhances performance, highlighting the efficacy of cognition-driven multimodal synthesis for speech-based AD detection.
relevance_note: LLM and TTS data augmentation for Alzheimer's disease detection; TTS is an augmentation tool for a clinical classification task, consistent with rejected TTS/VC-augmentation-for-classification precedents.
